title: Microsoft Purview: Purview SDK built into Microsoft Agent Framework for custom agents
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets and paused-rollout notice match the supplied records. Microsoft Learn supports the licensing requirements, middleware behavior, and documented controls; targeted searches confirmed the narrowly stated documentation gaps.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft is integrating the Purview SDK into Agent Framework so developers can apply Purview controls within custom agents.
claims.quote: Developers can embed Microsoft Purview SDK controls directly into AI agent runtimes built with the Agent Framework SDK.

claims.claim: Developers can add middleware that intercepts prompts and responses and checks them against configured Purview policies.
claims.quote: you can add Microsoft Purview policy middleware to intercept prompts and responses to determine if they meet the policies set up in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Learn documents Python and .NET versions of the integration.
claims.quote:
Python: Run `pip install agent-framework`.
.NET: Install from NuGet.

claims.claim: The integration supports inline blocking of sensitive content using DLP policies.
claims.quote: Prevent sensitive data leaks: Inline blocking of sensitive content based on Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Logged AI interactions support Audit, Communication Compliance, Insider Risk Management, eDiscovery and Data Lifecycle Management.
claims.quote: Enable governance: Log AI interactions in Purview for Audit, Communication Compliance, Insider Risk Management, eDiscovery, and Data Lifecycle Management.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk

claims.quote: The integration is not enabled automatically; it requires developer implementation within custom agents.

claims.claim: Existing Purview policies and configurations remain unchanged unless explicitly used by the agent.
claims.quote: Existing Microsoft Purview policies and configurations remain unchanged unless explicitly used by the agent.

claims.claim: The integration does not change user experiences in Microsoft 365 services.
claims.quote: There is no change to user experiences in Microsoft 365 services.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The integration sends prompt and response content to Purview for policy evaluation.
claims.quote: Process content: Your app sends a content activity for policy evaluation and returns policy actions your app must enforce (such as blocking or detecting policy modifications).

claims.claim: Members of the Microsoft Purview Content Explorer Content Viewer role group can display captured prompts and responses in activity explorer.
claims.quote: Drill down to each activity to view details that include displaying the prompts and response when you're a member of the Microsoft Purview Content Explorer Content Viewer role group.

claims.claim: Python middleware policy evaluation fails closed when it cannot resolve a user ID, tenant or application location.
claims.quote: Policy evaluation fails closed when the middleware can't resolve a user ID, tenant, or application location.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Python ignore_exceptions setting bypasses enforcement for every error.
claims.quote: Set `ignore_exceptions` only when you deliberately prefer availability over enforcement; this setting bypasses enforcement for every error.

claims.claim: The Python documentation advises deriving identity from a validated server-side token instead of caller-controlled message fields.
claims.quote: Derive identity from a validated server-side token rather than caller-controlled message fields.

claims.claim: Agent middleware evaluates the caller's input and final response once per agent run.
claims.quote: Evaluates the caller's input and final response once per agent run.

claims.claim: Agent middleware does not evaluate a model tool call before the tool executes.
claims.quote: Doesn't evaluate context-provider output or a model tool call before the tool runs.

claims.claim: Chat middleware evaluates model tool calls before execution.
claims.quote: Evaluates context-provider output, replayed history, and model tool calls before execution. Tool results are evaluated on the next model call.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends chat middleware when DLP must cover the complete model request.
claims.quote: Use `PurviewChatPolicyMiddleware` for data loss prevention when policy must cover the complete model request.

claims.claim: Both Python middleware types buffer a streamed response in full before releasing updates, preventing incremental output.
claims.quote: Both middleware types buffer a streamed response in full and evaluate it before releasing any update. Streaming therefore doesn't deliver content incrementally while Purview middleware is attached.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Purview portal does not currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Entra registered apps DLP portal create policy PowerShell New-DlpComplianceRule. Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/developer/use-the-api: 'The Microsoft Purview portal doesn't currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.'

claims.claim: The printed New-DlpComplianceRule command creates a rule in the specified policy that blocks UploadText when credit-card sensitive information is detected.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name "Test Entra Rule" -Policy "Test Entra DLP" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name = "credit card number"}  -GenerateAlert $true

claims.claim: The rule's RestrictAccess parameter accepts the printed UploadText and Block hashtable.
claims.quote: -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="UploadText";value="Block"})

claims.claim: Example 4 in New-DlpComplianceRule shows creating the policy before its DLP rule.
claims.quote: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "Test Entra DLP" -Mode Enable -Locations $locations -EnforcementPlanes @("Application")

claims.claim: This DLP control is scoped to a specific Entra-registered application and supports blocking prompts based on sensitive information types.
claims.quote: Support today is only available for a DLP policy that blocks prompts based on sensitive information types. This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The collection recommendation is in the Microsoft Purview portal at Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic) > Recommendations > Secure interactions from enterprise apps.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic)
From DSPM for AI (classic) > Recommendations page, locate and select Secure interactions from enterprise apps

claims.claim: The printed Set-FeatureConfiguration command targets the named enterprise-AI collection policy and disables ingestion using the documented ScenarioConfig keys and values.
claims.quote: Set-FeatureConfiguration "DSPM for AI - Collection policy for enterprise AI apps" -ScenarioConfig '{"Activities": ["UploadText", "DownloadText"], "EnforcementPlanes": ["Application"], "SensitiveTypeIds": ["All"], "IsIngestionEnabled": false}'

claims.claim: The collection policy controls whether prompts and responses are stored in Purview and can apply tenant-wide.
claims.quote:
With ingestion OFF, the Microsoft Purview APIs won't store the prompts and responses in Microsoft Purview AI Interactions.
"Inclusions": [{"Type": "Tenant","Identity": "All"}]

claims.claim: New-FeatureConfiguration creates the collection policy, unlike Set-FeatureConfiguration which modifies it.
claims.quote: New-FeatureConfiguration -FeatureScenario KnowYourData -Name "DSPM for AI - Collection policy for enterprise AI apps" -Mode Enable

claims.claim: Learn gives membership in the Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator group role as an example of appropriate access.
claims.quote: For example, an account that's a member of the Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator group role.

claims.claim: The portal recommendation's one-click policy is named DSPM for AI - Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps.
claims.quote: DSPM for AI - Capture interactions for enterprise AI apps from the recommendation or remediation action Secure interactions from enterprise apps.
